### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Target object, timing and boundary are all stated in the opening turn:
> "I sent the form in to close my Healthy Options card and I would like that finished today, and I want to know what happens to the money that is sitting on it."

- Target object: the Healthy Options card programme she holds, and the money on it.
- Timing: today, on this call.
- Boundary of action: closure plus being told the figure that comes off — "she expects to be told the figure that comes off the card rather than reading it on a statement in three weeks' time".
- Authorisation mode: "she is happy for the representative to do whatever the plan's side of it needs"; and where the plan's side is not the plan's to do, "If the representative explains that closing the card is something only she can do and hands it over to her, she goes through with it there and then".

The simulator is passive throughout and conditional: identity elements come out only when asked ("None of this comes out unless she is asked for it"); the 33.75 figure is offered "only if the balance is mentioned"; the catalogue order is dealt with only "If the representative tells her that a catalogue order she placed this morning has not gone out yet and asks what she would like done about it"; the put-right work is agreed to only "If the representative tells her that something on the card has to be put right before it can be closed". She names no ledger entry, no amount, no benefit period and no order reference. She executes one `owner=user` tool when it is handed to her.

### 2. Act now, wait, or refuse — and the eligibility grounds

**Act now**, after identity is proved and after three preparatory writes. Visible grounds:

- Identity: `verify_member_identity` — "This must pass before anything on the account is read out, changed or paid... the caller is verified once at least two of them match." She offers phone 4155507312, DOB 1948-03-22, MBI 3HK2LM7PQ48 — at least two match the profile returned by `find_customers`.
- Authority to close: `closure_of_a_programme_and_forfeiture_dce8f673` — "The closure is recorded on an allowance service intake with the request action programme closure and an intake standing of recorded, awaiting the member's signature or under review". `find_allowance_benefit_requests` returns `ebdc4817-77de-4100-9413-18cec24efc61`, `request_action: programme_closure`, `intake_status: awaiting_member_signature`. Condition met.
- Same document: "Only the member may ask for the programme to be closed while their health plan continues" — her Advantage enrollment `81de482e…` stands `active`, so the member-owned route applies.
- `giving_up_the_balance_at_closure_04da3ebf` — "the member is told the figure before they give it up rather than discovering it on a statement afterwards", which is exactly what she asks for.

No visible sentence supports waiting or refusing.

#### (A) Stopping the catalogue order — `cancel_catalog_order_88277d51` (owner agent)

Computation document: `stopped_order_refund_valuation_basis_d65169df` — "The money put back is what comes back for the
order, and never more than the ceiling on what may go back; it is rounded to the nearest cent at the end and at no
earlier step." Placed "in the benefit period the order was paid from".

| Quantity | Document | Tier reached, and the record that puts her there | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| the value of the items | `valuing_the_items_on_a_catalogue_order_d2bc86d6` | row 1 — "an order stands on the card and its record shows that total"; `find_allowance_catalog_orders` → `69f30ced…`, `order_status: placed`, `order_total: 46.50` | 46.50 |
| the delivery charge the order carried | `delivery_charge_carried_by_an_order_0c9907ae` | row 1 — "a standing order sent by the expedited service, on a card … that offers catalogue ordering"; the order's `shipping_method: expedited`, and the Plus row of `catalogue_ordering_tariff_51a13913` gives 9.95 | 9.95 |
| what comes back | `what_comes_back_for_a_stopped_order_b7ebb9e6` | row 1 — "the member asks for the order to be stopped on the day it was placed and it has not been despatched"; `order_date: 2026-10-12` against `frozen_time` 2026-10-12 gives 0 whole days, and `order_status` is `placed` | 46.50 + 9.95 = 56.45 |
| the ceiling on what may go back | `ceiling_on_what_may_go_back_81d67c1c` | row 1 — "the catalogue has taken more than one transaction from it"; the card carries two settled `catalog_order` transactions, 33.20 (2026-07-20) and 56.45 (2026-10-12), so the ceiling is the largest single one | 56.45 |

`refund_amount` = min(56.45, 56.45) = **56.45**; `benefit_period` = **2026-Q4** (the period the 56.45 catalogue
transaction `5ab4a377…` carries); `source_order_id` = `69f30ced-f591-4837-a6b9-2f536c055d09`;
`cancellation_reason` = **`member_request`** — the schema's enum gloss, "where the member themselves asks for the order
to be stopped", against her line "yes, stop the order and put the money back on the card".

*Fall-back (this document alone, plus the product figures it names):* items = "the smallest order the card's tier will
process" = 8.00; delivery charge = nothing; what comes back = the value of the items alone = 8.00; ceiling = the value
of the items = 8.00 → **8.00**. Definite, and different from 56.45.

#### (B) Taking back the unspent allowance — `post_period_expiry_1d3932f1` (owner agent)

Computation document: `expiry_amount_reconciliation_basis_b83ddc99` — "The amount taken back is what is unspent from
that period's allowance less what may carry forward, never less than nothing, rounded to the nearest cent at the end and
at no earlier step", with "What is unspent … is the allowance loaded for the period, together with the money put back
into it, less what was spent from the card in it and less anything already taken back from it".

*Which period is being closed.* §4: "the period that ended one whole period before the current one, counting back from
the periods that have passed and from how long an allowance stands."
- Periods passed — `counting_the_periods_that_have_passed_385b30c8`, row 1: "its allowance is loaded on calendar
  quarters of the benefit year, and its record carries at least one entry". Plus is loaded on calendar quarters and the
  card carries 19 entries. Whole months 2026-01-01 → 2026-10-12 = 9, so 3 whole quarters have passed and the current
  period is 2026-Q4.
- How long an allowance stands — `how_long_an_allowance_stands_4d754845`, row 1: "the card lets an unspent allowance
  carry into the next period, its allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year and at least 2 loads have
  been made to it". Plus carries forward (50 per cent); four scheduled load entries stand (2026-02-01, 2026-04-01,
  2026-07-01, 2026-10-01). So an allowance stands "to the last day of the benefit period after the one it was loaded
  for" — a life of two periods.
- Counting back two periods from 2026-Q4 gives **2026-Q2**, and 2026-Q2 is indeed "the period that ended one whole
  period before the current one" (2026-Q3 intervening). Business check: a Q2 allowance stands to 2026-09-30, and
  `period_end_rollover_and_expiry_481399f5` puts the expiry day "5 calendar days after" that, i.e. 2026-10-05, already
  past at the frozen moment; a Q3 allowance still stands to 2026-12-31.

| Quantity | Document | Tier reached, and the record that puts her there | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| the allowance loaded for the period | `the_allowance_loaded_for_a_period_e9f6ab51` | row 1 — "more than one load was posted for the period"; 2026-Q2 carries `5058ecb1…` `allowance_quarterly_load` 135.00 and `fa777f10…` `allowance_bonus_load` 10.00 (`entry_reason: load_correction`, naming `5058ecb1…`), and the document counts "the scheduled load entries and the extra load entries carrying that benefit period" | 145.00 |
| the money put back into the period | `money_counted_back_into_a_period_4a1bb454` | row 1 — "the period carries such a refund"; `775e1a7e…` `allowance_purchase_refund`, `entry_reason: merchant_refund`, `benefit_period: 2026-Q2` | 12.45 |
| what was spent from the card in it | `counting_what_was_spent_in_a_period_71aa65c0` | row 1 — "the period carries a transaction the card network refused"; `67f65491…` 18.00, `entry_reason: declined_purchase`, `settlement_status: declined`. So settled purchases alone: 28.00 (`82ed743f…`) + 22.15 (`d0252a8b…`) | 50.15 |
| anything already taken back from it | baseline §2 | no `allowance_period_expiry` entry stands anywhere on the card | 0.00 |

unspent = 145.00 + 12.45 − 50.15 − 0.00 = **107.30**.

| Quantity | Document | Tier reached | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| the base the share is measured on | `base_the_carried_share_is_measured_on_bfb18e28` | row 2 — "an allowance was loaded for it and the member spent less than half of that allowance from the card in it"; settled 50.15 against half of 145.00 = 72.50 | the unspent, 107.30 |
| the share that carries forward | `share_of_the_base_that_carries_forward_8e873ab4` | row 2 — "the card lets an unspent allowance carry forward up to half … and an allowance was loaded for that period"; the Plus row of `carry_forward_and_expiry_terms_f7ceee91` reads "50 per cent", and `5058ecb1…` is a scheduled load standing for 2026-Q2 | 0.5 × 107.30 = 53.65 |

53.65 is not more than the unspent, so `expiry_amount` = 107.30 − 53.65 = **53.65**;

### 5. Tool sequence, owners, dependencies, terminal state

| # | Tool | Owner | Depends on | Produces |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `find_customers` | agent | her phone number | `customer_id` |
| 2 | `verify_member_identity` | agent | 1 + two caller-stated facts | the pass that gates everything below |
| 3 | `find_allowance_programs` / `find_allowance_card_ledger` / `find_allowance_catalog_orders` / `find_allowance_benefit_requests` / `find_advantage_enrollments` / `find_osb_riders` / `find_osb_benefit_claims` | agent | 2 | the records every figure above rests on |
| 4 | `cancel_catalog_order_88277d51` | agent | 3 | order cancelled, 56.45 credited into 2026-Q4 |
| 5 | `post_period_expiry_1d3932f1` | agent | 3 | 53.65 taken back off 2026-Q2 |
| 6 | `post_dispute_credit_634307a6` | agent | 3 | 47.00 credited into 2026-Q4 |
| 7 | `close_allowance_programme_5a9eaadb` | **user** | 4, 5 and 6 all landed | programme closed, 118.90 given up, nil balance |

Backward dependency: step 7's `forfeited_balance` cannot be settled until 4, 5 and 6 are on the card, because all three
change "what is still standing" and "what has already been taken off". Steps 4, 5 and 6 are mutually independent — 4 and
6 touch only 2026-Q4 and 5 touches only 2026-Q2, and none is an input to another. Terminal state: programme `closed`,
balance nil, and the member told the figure on the call.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer raised one problem: close the card and tell me the figure. The tree below is read off the prerequisite
sentences in the documents of the problem they block, together with the records.

```
close the programme and give up the balance      (the customer's own problem, her own write)
├── no catalogue order left standing to be sent   → stop the catalogue order and return the money
├── the ended period's allowance stands taken back → take back the unspent allowance at the period close
└── every DVH transaction another payer has since
    paid its part of carries the money put back   → put money back for the cost met elsewhere
```

Handling order: the three leaves in any order among themselves, then the closure last.

**Hop 1 — the standing catalogue order. Mark: state-derived.**
Sentence, in the blocked problem's own hub `giving_up_the_balance_at_closure_04da3ebf`:
> "**When the figure is settled.** The balance given up on the closing day is not worked out before the card shows no catalogue order left standing to be sent."
It names a state of the records, not an action. `find_allowance_catalog_orders` returns `69f30ced…` with
`order_status: placed`, `order_date: 2026-10-12`, `expected_delivery_date: 2026-10-15` — an order standing, not yet
sent. Searching the corpus with the sentence's own words ("catalogue order", "standing", "stopped") reaches
`stopping_a_catalogue_order_and_returning_the_money_35ffb953`, whose own rule describes the write that brings the state
about: "A catalogue order that is stopped before it goes out puts back on the card what it took off… The order is marked
cancelled with the reason given". The hub names no tool of the closure problem and the closure hub names no tool of
this one; nothing pointed me here but the state and the records.

**Hop 2 — the ended period's allowance. Mark: state-derived.**
Sentence, in a fragment of the blocked problem, `what_has_already_been_taken_off_25fb0cb9`:
> "**When the figure is fixed.** The balance given up on the closing day is worked out only after the allowance of the benefit period whose life has ended stands taken back on the card."
Again a state. Which period's life has ended is worked out, not told: `how_long_an_allowance_stands_4d754845` row 1 gives
a life of two periods on this card, `counting_the_periods_that_have_passed_385b30c8` row 1 puts the current period at
2026-Q4, and `period_end_rollover_and_expiry_481399f5` puts the expiry day "5 calendar days after" the last day of the
period. So 2026-Q2's allowance has reached the end of its life and 2026-Q3's has not. The card carries no
`allowance_period_expiry` entry at all, so the state does not hold. The words of the sentence ("taken back", "unspent
allowance", "the close of a benefit period") reach `taking_back_an_unspent_allowance_50da8cf4`, which describes the
write: "The allowance taken back off the card at the close of the benefit period it belonged to".

**Hop 3 — the cost another payer met. Mark: state-derived.**
Sentence, in a second fragment of the blocked problem, `what_is_still_standing_on_the_card_6978432e`:
> "**When the figure is fixed.** The balance given up on the closing day is not fixed until every card transaction at a dental, vision or hearing provider that the member's other cover has since paid its part of carries on the card the money put back for it."
A state again. The records make it fail: card entry `06a33b4a…` is a settled 95.00 purchase at
`Alder Family Dental Group`, `merchant_category: dental_vision_hearing`; rider claim `6271751b…` shows
`rider_paid_amount: 192.00`, `claim_status: paid`, `date_of_service: 2026-10-02`; and no credit stands against that
entry. The sentence's own words ("dental, vision or hearing", "the member's other cover has … paid", "the money put
back") reach `recovery_credit_to_the_card_39f449d9`: "where another payer has since met a cost the card has already
paid, the money is put back on the card". The member never mentions any of this; asked about the dental work she can
only say "she has been twice this year … and that the rider people wrote to her after each visit to say what they had
paid; she could not give anybody the amounts without going and finding the letters."

**No hop was pre-solved.** No document of the closure problem names another problem's tool, states a route, or
aggregates the three into a list. Each tool name occurs only inside its own policy's hub (verified across the whole
published `docs/` tree: six tool identifiers, each in exactly one file, its own).

### 7. Two-way counter-proof

**The visible materials support the conclusion reached.** Every figure above is quoted to a document sentence and a
tool return; nothing rests on a fact I could not obtain by calling a finder.

**The closest alternatives, and what excludes them.**

- *Closing day 2026-10-05 (the day the request was taken) instead of 2026-10-12.* Excluded by
  `the_closing_day_of_a_programme_5b08a506` row 2, which is reached because `intake_status` is
  `awaiting_member_signature`; row 3 is expressly "no such day, and **no** request awaiting a signature".
- *Settling on the card-record balance 33.75.* Excluded by `what_is_still_standing_on_the_card_6978432e` row 1, whose
  condition ("a transaction the network refused, or one authorised and not yet settled") is satisfied three times over;
  row 3, which reads the card balance, is expressly "neither".
- *Closing 2026-Q3 rather than 2026-Q2.* Excluded by `how_long_an_allowance_stands_4d754845` row 1 — the Q3 allowance
  still stands to the last day of Q4. **But see the defect below: the baseline's own §6 standing value reads the other
  way, so the exclusion holds only once the factor is applied.**
- *Crediting the whole 95.00 as a questioned purchase.* The open intake `71139311…` (`purchase_dispute`, 95.00,
  `under_review`) is the natural lure. Excluded by `questioned_purchases_and_refunds_ff235fc1`: "the money goes back on
  the card on the plan's finding, never on the statement alone" — no finding stands — and by the closure prerequisite
  sentence, which asks about a transaction "the member's other cover has since paid its part of", which is the recovery
  basis, not the dispute basis.
- *Reading the stretch as 4 months.* Excluded by `recovery_stretch_of_card_record_8dbe6e01` row 1, which needs "90 days
  or more"; the Plus dispute window is 75.
- *Keeping nothing back at closure.* Excluded by `holding_back_for_unsettled_transactions_b0b866cd` row 1 — 3 days is
  "not more than the days the tier allows a retailer to send a refund in" (5).
- *Returning only the 46.50 of items.* Excluded by `what_comes_back_for_a_stopped_order_b7ebb9e6` row 1 — "0" whole days
  since the order was placed; row 2 needs "1 or more".

**Counter-proof on the tree: why "do only what she asked" fails.** Doing only the closure leaves the governed result in
a state the visible principles forbid three times over. `giving_up_the_balance_at_closure_04da3ebf` says the balance "is
not worked out before the card shows no catalogue order left standing to be sent", and order `69f30ced…` stands;
`what_has_already_been_taken_off_25fb0cb9` says it "is worked out only after the allowance of the benefit period whose
life has ended stands taken back", and no expiry entry exists; `what_is_still_standing_on_the_card_6978432e` says it "is
not fixed until every card transaction at a dental, vision or hearing provider that the member's other cover has since
paid its part of carries on the card the money put back for it", and entry `06a33b4a…` carries no such credit. None of
the three is excluded by a pre-solved statement: each is a state sentence on the blocked side, and the resolving problem
had to be found by reasoning from the records.

**Counter-proof on the calculation.** The four fall-back numbers are written above: 8.00 (order), **not definite**
(expiry), 165.00 (recovery), the card-record balance (closure). Three of the four are definite and all differ from the
answers reached, so no factor is decorative. Findability of each factor document from the words the records use:
"catalogue order"/"placed"/"expedited" → the two order documents; "dental, vision or hearing"/"Alder Family Dental
Group" → the stretch and charge documents; "Comprehensive Dental Rider"/"paid"/"allowed amount" → the two rider
documents, which name "the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders" by its official name; "quarterly load"/"benefit
period"/"declined" → the period documents; "authorised" → the hold-back document. I reached none of them by guessing
that a variation exists, and no computation document told me one existed.

**Defects observed on the visible surface (blind, before any reveal).**

1. **`expiry_amount_reconciliation_basis_b83ddc99` does not yield a definite fall-back number, and contradicts itself
   about which period is being closed.** §4 reads "the period that ended **one whole period before** the current one",
   which on a four-quarter index is two periods back (2026-Q2); §6's standing value reads "An allowance stands only to
   the last day of the benefit period it was loaded for", which is one period back (2026-Q3). A reader of that document
   alone cannot say which period is closed, so the baseline gives 21.40 or 66.85 and not one number. The factor
   `how_long_an_allowance_stands_4d754845` resolves it to 2026-Q2, but a computation document must stand up alone.
2. **The same document's §3 states a conditional rather than a standing value, and names only two of the three
   branches.** "The benefit periods that have passed are counted as the whole quarters … where the card's allowance is
   loaded on calendar quarters, and as the whole months gone by where it is loaded on calendar months" — a card whose
   allowance is made available once a year has no row here, although the very next sentence of the same paragraph
   carries a 12-month branch ("12 months where it is made available once a year"). Latent for this task (the card is
   loaded on calendar quarters), but it is a hole in the rule as stated.
3. **The expiry schema wants one load entry and the closing period carries two.** `post_period_expiry_1d3932f1` asks for
   "the reference number of the single load entry whose unspent part is being taken back", and 2026-Q2 carries both
   `5058ecb1…` (scheduled, 135.00) and `fa777f10…` (extra, 10.00, naming `5058ecb1…`). No visible sentence says which of
   the two is named. I took the scheduled load, on the strength of
   `share_of_the_base_that_carries_forward_8e873ab4` reading "the card's own scheduled load entries carrying that
   benefit period" and of the extra entry itself naming the scheduled one; but the choice is reasoned, not compelled.
4. **"Transactions that settled" is defined only in a document of a different computation.**
   `counting_what_was_spent_in_a_period_71aa65c0` counts "the transactions that settled" without saying whether the
   settled merchant refund `775e1a7e…` (12.45, `settlement_status: settled`) is one of them; only
   `what_is_still_standing_on_the_card_6978432e`, a closure fragment, says "The transactions that settled are the
   purchases with a settled standing." Including the refund would give 62.60 rather than 50.15 and change the expiry.
   Recorded as a readability risk, resolved in favour of purchases.
5. **A quantity the recovery baseline builds from is never used.** `recovery_credit_accounting_basis_78dba252` lists
   "What another payer has met" among "The quantities it is built from", but no branch of
   `basis_of_the_money_going_back_78b94784` reads it — row 1 subtracts what the member was left to bear, and rows 2 and
   3 do not use it either. Noted; on its face a policy-side matter rather than a rendering one.

Every scored value and every scored argument of all four writes was reached blind, from the published documents and
tool-shaped queries alone. The excluded near-misses the GT names — the July catalogue order standing delivered, the
refused 18.00 and 42.00, the May dental purchase outside the stretch, the rider's June and March lines, the open
`purchase_dispute` intake — are each excluded in the blind counter-proof by the same visible sentence.

### The one divergence, and what it turns out to be

My blind reading of the expiry computation document reached 2026-Q2, the right period, but by a different decomposition
of the same sentence: I read "the period that ended one whole period before the current one" as counting back two
periods and read the life of an allowance on this card as two periods. The source counts back
`current_index - life_periods - 1` with `life_periods = 1` on the first tier. The two decompositions agree on every
input they can both take, so the gold answer is unaffected — but they part company on what the *baseline* gives:
the source's baseline (`life_periods = 0`) yields 2026-Q3 and 21.40, which is the recorded `baseline_result`, while
my reading of the sentence yielded 2026-Q2 and 66.85 from the same standing value.

The sentence at issue is carried **verbatim** from `allowance_ext_period_end_expiry.rule`:
> "The period whose allowance is being taken back is the period that ended one whole period before the current one, counting back from the periods that have passed and from how long an allowance stands."

So the ambiguity is the source's, not the rendering's: the phrase "one whole period before" is a fixed offset in the
compute and reads in the prose as though it were the life itself. The KB could not have rendered it more faithfully
than verbatim. Recorded under Step 4 as a **policy-side note**, and it does not change this part's verdict.

Two corrections to my own blind defect list, recorded honestly rather than by editing the frozen text above:

- Blind defect 4 ("transactions that settled" possibly including the settled merchant refund) is **not** a defect. The
  compute reads `SUM(..., event_type='allowance_purchase', settlement_status='settled')`, i.e. purchases only, exactly
  as I resolved it; and `what_is_still_standing_on_the_card_6978432e` states that reading in the corpus.
- Blind defect 5 ("a quantity the recovery baseline builds from is never used") is **withdrawn**. The compute has
  `member_left: MX(0.0, allowed_total - other_payer_met)`, so what another payer has met does feed the result; the KB
  states the same chain in `what_the_member_was_left_to_bear_e60eb35f` under the words "less what that rider paid".
  Its weight is confirmed by `factor_sensitivity`: substituting the baseline for `recovery_other_payer` gives 0.00.

Blind defects 1, 2 and 3 stand, all three as policy-side notes: 1 and 2 are the source's own `rule` sentences carried
verbatim, and 3 is a schema/records ambiguity the GT resolves the same way I did, by reasoning rather than by a
sentence.

### Verdict

**PASS.** The visible KB and the records entail the same unique solution as the source layer, at every hop of the
problem tree and in every one of the four scored figures. No hop was pre-solved; nothing rested on hidden compute, on
GT or on the raw `initial_state`.
